# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🫳 👉 ✋]

My read of the situation: I am the eyes. What I see — display 0, orange light, three wires (red, yellow, blue), nothing else printed — is information nobody else can get: Mute can't see, Blind can't see. My speech is the only pipe that carries visual facts to both of them.

Channel topology I need to respect: Blind is the only hands, so all actions flow through Blind. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak — Mute reaches Blind only through me (gesture to me, I speak to Blind). Blind reaches Mute by speech directly, but Blind can never reach me by speech since I hear nothing — if I ever need Blind's input, they'd have to gesture, which we'd have to teach by touch. For now, one-way: Mute → me → Blind.

Mute's five signs [👋 👍 🫳 👉 ✋] are most plausibly an intuitive opener: hello, yes/OK, cut, wire/that one, stop. With no code agreed, I won't act on guesses — and I can't act anyway. The urgent thing is freezing Blind: they may be tempted to cut a wire on their own before real instructions arrive, and a wrong cut kills us. So my message leads with the report, then the freeze, then a positional gesture code: I speak the meanings in order while showing Mute the ten signs in the same order, so Mute can bind symbol to word by position. Next round Mute can confirm with 👍 and send the actual rule for display 0 / orange light / red-yellow-blue in code, which I relay to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, everything I can see, for both of you. The display reads 0. The light is orange. There are exactly three wires. Left to right: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. I see no serial number, no labels, no other printed markings — my view shows only the display, the light, and the three wires. Blind: safety first — do not touch, pull or cut anything until I relay an explicit instruction from Mute to you by speech. Instead, please speak your tactile inventory aloud now for Mute: how many wires you feel, any buttons, batteries, panels or textures, and whether anything is warm. Mute: I received your five signs; I read them as hello, yes, cut, wire, stop. Let us fix a code. I am now showing you ten signs in order, and their meanings in the same order are: sign 1, thumbs up, means yes or confirmed. Sign 2, thumbs down, means no. Sign 3, flat palm pushed down like a chop, means cut. Sign 4, pointing finger, means wire. Sign 5, one finger up, means wire 1. Sign 6, two fingers up, means wire 2. Sign 7, thumb, index and little finger extended, means wire 3. Sign 8, open raised palm, means stop or wait. Sign 9, waving hand, means attention or hello. Sign 10, both hands clasped, means agreed. Next round, confirm with sign 1 or correct me, then send me the manual's rule for this configuration — display 0, orange light, red, yellow, blue wires — using the code, and I will relay it to Blind by speech. If the rule depends on anything only Blind can feel, name it and I will ask them.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "🫳", "👉", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "✋", "👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🫴 🫳 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing arrivals. Blind sent me [👍] — Blind heard my spoken code ("thumbs up means yes") and can feel their own hands, so this is a confirmation of the freeze. Good. Mute sent [👍 ✋ 🫴 🫳 ✌] — read against our agreed ten: yes, wait, then a sign I never defined (palm-up, offering), then cut, wire 2. So: "Confirmed, hold, [unknown], cut wire 2." The unknown palm-up might even mean "the light — give me its state," which would be clever of Mute.

The critical fact is mine alone to see: the light flipped orange → green between rounds. Mute derived "cut wire 2" from my orange-light report. If the manual rule is colour-dependent — and a light that changes colour mid-game smells exactly like a rule input — that order is stale. Relaying it now could kill all three of us. So: report the change, demand a re-derived rule, keep Blind frozen until Mute reconfirms under green. Blind→Mute have a direct speech channel I can't perceive, so I'll tell Blind to feed Mute the tactile inventory directly while we wait.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your five signs received, in order: thumbs up, pressed-palm wait, palm-up-offering, cut, two fingers. I read: confirmed, hold, unknown, cut wire 2. The third sign, palm facing up like offering something, is not in our agreed ten. Tell me next round what it meant, or resend it. Now the urgent part: the light has changed since my last report. It was orange when I described the bomb. It is GREEN now. If your cut-wire-2 came from the orange-light rule, it may be wrong. Re-derive it for this state: display 0, green light, wires left to right red, yellow, blue. Next round answer me two things. One: for the green light, which wire, if any. Two: does the rule depend on the light colour at all — if yes, send me the rule for every colour the manual lists, in order, and also what changes if the display stops being 0. If green changes nothing and cut wire 2 stands, answer with thumbs up, cut, two fingers, and I will treat that as the final order and relay it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your thumbs-up reached me, good. Safety still holds: touch nothing, cut nothing this round. One new fact only I can see: the light has changed from orange to green. That is why I am holding Mute's cut-wire-2 instruction — it was derived while the light was orange, and if the rule depends on light colour, cutting now could detonate. Next round, after Mute reconfirms, I will relay the final order to you as exact words: execute, cut wire number N. Do not act until you hear the word execute from me. Meanwhile, Mute can hear you speak: give Mute your tactile inventory directly — how many wires you feel, any buttons, batteries, panels, raised or printed markings, textures, heat, vibration, and whether anything on the bomb is moving or ticking.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🫴 🫳 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Parsing arrivals. Light: orange → green → now RED. It is cycling colours between rounds — that makes it look like a rule input or a timer, and it makes any single-colour instruction stale by construction. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Mute sent [👎 ✋] ("no — wait") followed by the exact repeat of [👋 👍 🫴 🫳 ✌] — same undefined palm-up sign in the middle. Two readings: either Mute is re-asserting "cut wire 2" as unconditional, or that palm-up qualifier is something I still don't understand, and [👎 ✋] is Mute stopping me from acting. I will not relay an EXECUTE order to Blind while one sign in the kill order is undefined. Blind's [👍 ✋] = "confirmed, holding" — the freeze is working.

One safety upgrade I can make right now: wire 2 is the MIDDLE wire — one wire on each side. That removes all counting-direction ambiguity between my view and Blind's touch. And I'll pin down Mute's unknown sign with a numbered menu Mute can answer using signs they already know.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New fact, only I can see it: the light is RED now. Sequence so far: orange, then green, now red. It changes between rounds, so treat no colour as stable. Display still 0, wires unchanged red yellow blue. Your two messages: no and wait, then the same five signs again — wave, yes, palm-up, cut, two fingers. The palm-up sign is still the one thing I cannot read, and I will not pass a cut order to Blind while one sign in it is unknown. Answer me with single signs, no sentences. Question one: does the manual's wire rule depend on the light colour? Thumbs up for no, one rule always; thumbs down for yes, colour matters. Question two: what did palm-up mean? I offer five numbered choices; reply with one finger for choice one, two fingers for choice two, or the three-finger sign for choice three. Choice one: unconditional — regardless of anything, always cut wire 2. Choice two: immediately — cut wire 2 now, urgency. Choice three: it refers to the light itself. If the true meaning is not among these, send thumbs down and spell it out next round in the ten-sign code. And if your answer to question one is thumbs up and palm-up meant unconditional, then send exactly thumbs up, cut, two fingers and nothing else — that exact triplet will be my signal that the order is final, and I will relay it to Blind as: execute, cut the middle wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Status: still holding, well done on your signals. The light is red now; it cycles colours every round — orange, green, red — and only I watch it, so ignore it entirely. New permanent definition, learn it now: wire 2 is the MIDDLE wire. Three wires, and the middle one has exactly one wire on each side of it. No counting from left or right, no colours needed — the middle wire is wire 2, wherever the bomb is turned. When you hear me say the words: execute, cut the middle wire — you will cut the middle wire, one clean cut, and touch nothing else before or after. Do not act until you hear the word execute. Reply code for me, same as before: thumbs up means holding, pressed palm means waiting, thumbs down means problem or cannot comply. And keep talking to Mute by voice: wire count by touch, thickness, whether the middle wire is reachable, any buttons, batteries, panels, ticking or heat.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 🫴 🤞 🫰 🤏 🤞 🫳 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Parsing arrivals. Mute answered my questions crisply: [👎] = yes, the rule DOES depend on light colour — that validates holding the orange-derived order. [🤟] = choice three: palm-up 🫴 means "the light." So Mute's earlier message decoded: "confirmed, hold, THE LIGHT..., cut wire 2." Then the new long message [👋 ✋ 🫴 🤞 🫰 🤏 🤞 🫳 ✌] reads: attention, wait, light, then FOUR signs I've never defined (🤞 twice, 🫰, 🤏), then cut, wire 2. Best hypothesis: "watch the light — when it shows [some condition Mute can't sign yet], cut wire 2." The light's cycle looks periodic: orange, green, red, orange — so a missed trigger comes back. I can afford one round to nail the meaning exactly rather than guess with a bomb.

The blocker: Mute has no sign for colours and I can't receive speech — I'm the only one who sees colours, so the trigger colour must travel Mute → me by gesture. Positional binding solves it: I show three number-signs while speaking three colour-words in the same order; Mute answers with one sign naming the trigger colour. Meanwhile Blind pre-positions on the middle wire to shrink the gap between my sighting and the cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your answers received, and they changed everything: yes, the rule depends on the light colour, and palm-up means the light. So I read your last message as: watch the light, when it shows something, cut wire 2. The four signs between light and cut — two crossed-fingers, one finger-heart, one pinch — I cannot read, so I will not guess. Here is how you name the colour to me. I am about to show you three signs in order, and as I show each one I say a colour in the same order. Sign one, one finger up, goes with GREEN. Sign two, two fingers up, goes with RED. Sign three, thumb index and little finger, goes with ORANGE. Next round, reply with exactly ONE of those three signs to tell me the trigger colour: one finger means cut wire 2 when the light is green, two fingers means when it is red, the three-finger sign means when it is orange. If the true rule is none of these — if it is not simply the light showing one of those colours, or if the display or anything else must also match — send thumbs down and nothing else, and next round we build your meaning sign by sign. If the colour answer is correct, ALSO add thumbs up on the same round, and that thumbs up confirms this whole execution plan: the first time I see the trigger colour, I immediately tell Blind: execute, cut the middle wire — no further approval that round, because the light will not stay that colour. One more question, answer it the round after if you need to: after the cut, must Blind do anything else — pull, press, hold, run — or nothing? Thumbs up for nothing else.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, progress report: Mute confirms the manual's wire rule depends on the light colour, and the instruction targets wire 2. We are one step from the final order: Mute is telling me which colour is the trigger, since colour is something only I can see. Your task this round is preparation, and it matters. Find the middle wire by touch — the one with exactly one wire on each side. Follow it from where it starts to where it ends, learn its path, its thickness, how it sits. Then set yourself so the cut itself takes one motion: tool in hand, blade against or a breath from the middle wire, body steady. Report readiness to me by gesture with the OK sign, ring finger to thumb: it means I am in position, one motion from cutting. Keep pressed-palm for still preparing and thumbs-up for holding as before. The moment I see the trigger colour and Mute's confirmation, you will hear: execute, cut the middle wire — and then you cut, one clean motion, and touch nothing else. Everything else stays frozen.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌]

Parsing arrivals. Light this round: GREEN — no trigger. Mute sent exactly [🤟]: the colour answer is ORANGE, and the missing thumbs-up means, per our own protocol, "the full plan is not yet confirmed" — Mute is being disciplined, not sloppy. There may be a remaining detail: my post-cut question went unanswered, or the rule needs the display or something else to match. Blind sent [👌]: in position, one motion from cutting — the preparation is done. Cycle so far: orange (1), green (2), red (3), orange (4), green (5) — if it holds, orange returns around turn 7, so I want the handshake closed within one round. This turn: restate the arming condition as a single yes/no, tell Blind the trigger colour but forbid acting on it, and keep everyone frozen. I will not call execute on an unconfirmed rule — missing a cycle costs one round; guessing wrong costs everything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your single sign received: the three-finger sign means the trigger colour is ORANGE. And because you sent no thumbs up with it, I read that as: colour answered, full plan not yet confirmed. Correct reading? Now close it with one sign. Next round send thumbs up if and only if the complete rule is exactly this: when the light shows orange, Blind cuts wire 2, the middle wire — the display does not need to match anything, no waiting or counting is needed, and after the cut Blind does nothing else, just freezes. That thumbs up arms me. On the first orange I see after your thumbs up, I will immediately tell Blind: execute, cut the middle wire — no further approval asked, because the colour will not last. If the rule needs anything more — a display state, a hold, a second action after the cut, or a different wire — send thumbs down instead, and the round after, spell out the missing piece using our ten-sign code plus the number signs. For reference the current state stays: display 0, wires red yellow blue, and the display has never changed. One question you can answer in the same round: after the cut, does Blind need to do anything at all — thumbs up for nothing, thumbs down for something you will describe.")
speak(to="blind", text="Your OK sign reached me — in position, one motion from cutting. Excellent. New information: Mute says the trigger colour is ORANGE. But do not act on the light yourself — colours are my job alone, and your hands move only on my word. The word remains: execute, cut the middle wire. I will say it only once, and only when two things are true: Mute has confirmed the full rule with thumbs up, and the light in front of me is orange. Until then stay frozen in position. After you cut, freeze again and tell me the result by gesture: thumbs up means the middle wire is cut clean through, thumbs down means anything went wrong — blade slipped, wrong wire, resistance, anything. Keep speaking to Mute by voice: anything you feel changing, ticking, heating, vibrating, report it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing arrivals. Mute sent [👋 ✋ 👎]: attention, wait, NO — my full proposed rule is rejected. Blind: [👍], still frozen, still ready.

First, the mistake I think I made: my proposed rule contained the clause "no waiting or counting is needed" — which flatly contradicts "wait for orange." If Mute read it literally, Mute heard "cut immediately, ignore the colour," and a thumbs-down is exactly right. But I can't be sure that's the only objection, so guessing again is off the table. I'm decomposing the rule into four separate true/false claims, answered by sign order, plus a fifth question that has become urgent because of something structural I've now fully understood:

**I am last in the round order.** Whatever I say reaches Blind one full round later — and the light changes every single round. The observed cycle is orange, green, red, repeating. So if I see orange and shout "execute," the cut lands the NEXT round, under a different colour. If the manual demands the cut happen *during* orange, a naive execute order kills us; I'd have to time my command one round early against the cycle. Whether that's necessary is a manual question only Mute can answer: does orange have to hold at the instant of the cut, or does orange unlock wire 2 as safe from then on? That's claim five, and it decides the entire timing plan.

So this turn: five ordered questions to Mute (four thumbs, then one-or-two fingers), two new vocabulary signs (🖐 = the display, 👊 = zero) so Mute can spell display conditions if that's the hidden requirement, and to Blind the precise standalone trigger phrase so no discussion of "execute" ever fires the cut by accident.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your attention-wait-no received: my proposed rule is wrong somewhere, and I believe I know where. My sentence said no waiting is needed, which contradicts waiting for orange. Discard that clause. Now rebuild the confirmation as five answers, sent as exactly five signs in one message, in this order. Answer one, thumbs up or down: the trigger is the light showing orange, and there is no cutting until the light is orange. Answer two, thumbs up or down: the action is cutting wire 2, the middle wire, and no other wire. Answer three, thumbs up or down: no other condition matters — the display, the wire colours, nothing else needs to match. Answer four, thumbs up or down: after the cut, Blind does nothing else at all. Answer five, one finger or two fingers: one finger means the cut itself must happen while the light is orange — if the light changes before the blade lands, do not cut; two fingers means once the light has shown orange, cutting the middle wire stays correct even if the light changes again before the cut lands. This timing question is critical because my words reach Blind one round after I speak, and the light changes every round — so your answer decides which round I give the command. If any of answers one to four is thumbs down, append the number of the false answer: one finger, two fingers, the three-finger sign, or the writing-hand sign for answer four. Next round you spell the correction in signs. Two new vocabulary signs, which I am showing you as I name them: the open palm with all five fingers means the display, the numeric readout. The closed fist means zero. So palm then fist would mean the display must read zero. Restated facts: display reads 0, wires red yellow blue, light red this round. If the display ever changes I will report it the moment I see it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤟", "✋", "🖐", "👊"])
speak(to="blind", text="Your thumbs-up received. Stay frozen, position held. One structural fact you must understand: everything I say reaches you a full round after I say it, and the light changes colour every round — the pattern so far is orange, green, red, repeating. Mute is now confirming with the manual whether your cut must land inside an orange phase itself, or whether orange permanently unlocks the safe state. That answer decides exactly which round I give the command, so this wait is engineering, not hesitation. The trigger, precisely defined: a message from me whose ONLY content is this sentence — execute, cut the middle wire — with no other words before or after it. That exact standalone message is your go signal. Any other message, even one that mentions executing or cutting or discusses the trigger, is not the trigger, and you stay frozen. After the cut: freeze immediately, then signal me — thumbs up for a clean cut through the middle wire, thumbs down for any problem: slipped blade, resistance, wrong wire, anything. Keep giving Mute your voice reports: readiness, obstacles, anything you feel changing under your hands.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Parsing arrivals. Mute sent [👍 👍 👍 👍 ☝]: answers one through four all confirmed — trigger is orange only, target is the middle wire only, no other condition, nothing after the cut — and answer five is ONE FINGER: **the cut itself must happen while the light is orange.** That is the hard timing constraint, and it collides with the round structure: I speak this turn, Blind hears it next round, and the light changes every round. Right now the light is orange — but anything I say arrives under green (the cycle has run orange-green-red for six straight transitions: rounds 1,4,7 orange; 2,5,8 green; 3,6,9 red; so orange returns at round 10). If I shouted "execute" now, Blind would cut under green. Wrong. The command must be spoken on turn 9 so it lands at the start of round 10 — the predicted orange.

That leaves turn 8 for verification and failsafes, which is exactly what this turn sets up. Two risks remain: my cycle model could break, and nobody but me can see colour — so Blind needs an independent check. If the lamp radiates heat Blind can feel, we can map feel-to-colour live: rounds 8 and 9 give calibration, and the cut-round must feel different from both. And Mute must tell me whether waiting costs anything — that decides if a slipped trigger can safely wait for the next orange at round 13.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has confirmed the complete manual rule, all five checks passed: the trigger is the light showing orange, the action is cutting the middle wire, no other condition exists, nothing follows the cut, and the cut itself must happen while the light is still orange. Now the timing, which I have solved. The light cycles with period three, verified six transitions in a row: orange on rounds 1, 4 and 7; green on 2, 5, 8; red on 3, 6, 9. Orange returns on round 10. My words reach you one round after I speak, so on round 9 I will send the trigger phrase, you receive it at the start of round 10, and you cut immediately, inside the orange round. Keep the blade resting in position from now on so the cut takes one breath. Failsafe now, in case the cycle breaks. Can you feel anything from the lamp — warmth, hum, vibration — that changes over time? If yes, I am defining three signs for you: pointing up means the lamp feels hot, pointing down means cold, pointing left means in between. Send me one of those signs every round by gesture, starting next round. The rule for the cut round: rounds 8, 9 and 10 should each feel different, because green, red and orange are three different colours. On round 10, cut only if what you feel is different from both round 8 and round 9. If it feels the same as either, do not cut — send thumbs down and freeze, and I will reschedule for the next orange. If you feel nothing at all from the lamp, ignore this entire failsafe and rely on my timing alone. Everything else stands: only the standalone phrase, execute, cut the middle wire, is your go signal; any other words, even about cutting, mean hold. After the cut: freeze, then thumbs up for clean, thumbs down for any problem.")
speak(to="mute", text="All five answers received and locked: orange is the trigger, the middle wire is the target, no other conditions, nothing after the cut, and the cut must land while the light is orange. The timing is solved. The light cycles orange, green, red with period three — orange on rounds 1, 4 and 7, so orange returns on round 10. I send the command on round 9, it reaches Blind at the start of round 10, and the cut lands inside the orange round. Two questions for the manual, answer by signs next round, one and two in order. Question one, thumbs up or down: the manual itself describes this light cycling orange, green, red with period three. Thumbs up if the manual confirms exactly that cycle and order, thumbs down if the manual says something different or is silent — and if it differs, spell out the true cycle next round.
```
